title: A Simple-to-Use BDI Architecture for Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation

key_points.claim: Social simulations have grown more realistic, but most agent architectures are still simple reactive models (agent cognition aspect).
key_points.evidence_quote: most agent architectures in these simulations use simple reactive models.

key_points.claim: Cognitive architectures face two obstacles: complexity for field-expert modelers and computational cost.
key_points.evidence_quote: Cognitive architectures face two main obstacles: their complexity for the field-expert modeler, and their computational cost.

key_points.claim: The authors propose a BDI architecture integrated into GAMA, written in GAML, designed to be simple, flexible and computationally cheap.
key_points.evidence_quote: a new cognitive agent architecture based on the Belief-Desire-Intention paradigm integrated into the GAMA modeling platform

key_points.claim: The architecture is illustrated with a land-use evolution model of the Mekong Delta (environment/land-use aspect).
key_points.evidence_quote: illustrated with a simulation of the evolution of land-use in the Mekong Delta.

reliability_notes: Abstract only (paywalled preview). Peer-reviewed chapter by Taillandier et al. (University of Rouen). No full-text details or results were available.
